credits.readme:
The box: *Food Box with Striped Decoration and Chinese Figures*, Japan, Edo period, 17th century. The Metropolitan
Museum of Art, 2015.500.2.31a–f, Gift of Florence and Herbert Irving, 2015. Open Access, CC0. Photographs
`L1996_47_86_O2_sf` … `O6_sf`.

Prints: Utagawa Hiroshige, *Uozukushi*: "Medetai Fish and Sasaki Bamboo", "Ise-ebi and Shiba-ebi", "Kurodai and
Kodai Fish with Bamboo Shoots and Berries" (The Met, DP123587, DP123581, DP123580; CC0). "Basket of Lotus Root and
Single String Chin", surimono, Japan, 19th century (LACMA M.79.152.573, public domain). All via Wikimedia Commons.

Matting: this repo's asset engine (`tools/engine/stages/matte.py`, BiRefNet via rembg). Registration: OpenCV ECC.
The demo's restaurant, its prices and its addresses are invented.

YūzukiKyoto
KaisekiOsechiOrder

New Year 2027 · osechi ryōri

Five tiers for the first three days

Osechi is cooked before the year turns, so that no fire need be lit for the first three days. It comes packed in a jūbako, a box of stacked tiers, because good things should pile up.

一の重 Celebration

一の重 ichi-no-jū

The small things that make it a celebration, eaten first, with the first sake.

Kuromame black soybeans
Mame: to be hard-working, and well.
Kazunoko herring roe
Thousands of eggs: many children.
Tazukuri candied sardines
Once spread on the rice fields: a good harvest.
Datemaki rolled omelette
Rolled like a scroll: learning.
Kurikinton chestnut and sweet potato
Gold: a prosperous year.

二の重 From the grill

二の重 ni-no-jū

Fish and prawns from the grill, cooked the day before and eaten cool.

Tai sea bream
Medetai: joyful.
Ebi prawns
Long whiskers and a bent back: to live until bent with age.
Buri yellowtail
A fish that changes its name as it grows: to rise in the world.

三の重 Simmered

三の重 san-no-jū

Roots and shoots simmered together in one pot, so that a family stays together.

Renkon lotus root
Holes to see the year ahead through.
Satoimo taro
Small corms around a mother: many children.
Gobō burdock
A root that goes deep: a family settled.
Takenoko bamboo shoots
Growing fast and straight.

与の重 Vinegared

与の重 yo-no-jū

Never “the fourth”: four is shi, which also says death. This tier is yo, and holds the sharp, clean things.

Kōhaku namasu daikon and carrot
Red and white, like the cord on a gift.
Kikka kabu turnip
Cut into a chrysanthemum.

五の重 Kept empty

五の重 go-no-jū

The last tier is left empty: room for the good things the year will bring.

Ours comes empty too, lacquered and clean. Fill it with what your family likes, or leave it as it is.

Order by 26 December

For four, in a lacquered box

Packed on the morning of 31 December. The box is lent with the food, wrapped in a furoshiki.

¥54,000 for four · tax included

A deposit of ¥10,000 holds your box. The rest is paid when you collect it.

Collecting it

Collect

31 December, 9:00 to 15:00, at the side door on Tominokōji. Bring your reservation number.

Delivery

Within Kyoto city, ¥2,200, between 10:00 and 14:00 on the 31st.

Returning the box

By 15 January, washed by hand and dried, never soaked. The furoshiki is yours to keep.

# jubako Tabs that are the tiers of a Japanese food box. A *jūbako* of the 17th century (The Met 2015.500.2.31a–f) stands beside the tab list, one tier to a tab. Choose a tab, or take hold of a tier and draw it up, and the tiers above lift off along the box's own axis and hang there, so the tier you chose stands open and its panel comes out of the box's side, level with it; choose a higher one and they come back down onto it. Every tier is the Met's own photograph: the museum photographed this box five times from one camera, taking a tier off each time, so every inside you see open is the inside the photographer saw. For a menu by courses, a product page's details, a documentation section, a card with two to five views. The demo is a New Year *osechi* order page, which is what jūbako are for: one course to a tier. ```html
…

一の重 Celebration

…

二の重 From the grill

…
``` Keep the six `` exactly as above (bottom tier first): their places are measured (`assets/geometry.json`). ## What it does - **A real tablist.** The JS makes a `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons from the panels' `.jb-head` headings (or uses a `.jb-tabs` you wrote), with `aria-controls`, `aria-selected`, roving `tabindex`; panels become `role="tabpanel"`, labelled by their tab and focusable. ↑ ↓ ← → move and choose (selection follows focus, as a tab set should when switching is instant), Home and End go to the first and last. The headings stay in the panels for screen readers and are hidden from sight; their markup (a ``) is carried into the tab. - **Quicker than a plain one.** The panel swaps at once; the box moves beside it and never holds the reader up. Pointing at a tab, the tiers that would move give a little toward where they would go. - **By hand.** Press a tier and draw upward: the tiers from it up come off in your hand, on a stiffer spring that follows it, and a little past the lift they resist. Let go past 40 % of the lift (or with a flick) and the tier under them is chosen; short of it, they settle back. Press a lifted tier and draw down to close the stack onto it. A press without a draw chooses the tier pressed. A finger rests 180 ms before it holds a tier (the tiers give a little to say so), so a swipe across the box still scrolls the page (`touch-action: pan-y`). A mouse holds at once. - **The panel comes out of its tier.** In the aside layout the chosen panel's top is set level with the open tier's mouth, and it slides out from the box's side (0.5 s, settling). On a phone it drops in under the box. - **Lacquer fits close.** As a stack comes off a tier, that tier is drawn up with it about 2 % of the lift and drops back, the way a snug lid takes the box with it for a moment. - **Without JS** the box stands with its top tier open and every panel is shown under its own heading, in order. - **Reduced motion:** the tiers are where they belong at once, the panel appears without sliding. A drag still moves what you hold. - **The motion** is springs: each tier a mass (ζ 0.8, ω 19 s⁻¹, fixed steps at 240 Hz) whose target is the lift for the tiers above the chosen one and 0 for the others, or the hand's height (ω 34 s⁻¹ while held). A tier never sinks into the one below it: it rides on it. Changing your mind mid-lift is continuous. The loop runs only while something moves, and not off screen. - **Two layouts, by measurement.** *Aside* (the component 760 px wide or more, and tiers at least 26 px apart): each tab sits beside its own tier, at the middle of the tier's band where it meets the box's right edge, and rides up with it; the panel is to the right, with an optional `.jb-title` above it. *List* (narrower: a phone, a card): a small box at the left with the tabs listed beside it in the tiers' order, and the panel under both. ## Options | option | data attribute | default | | |---|---|---|---| | `selected` | `data-selected` | URL `#hash` if it names a panel, else 0 | index (0-based) or panel id to start on; lands without moving | | `lift` | `data-lift` | `0.8` | how far lifted tiers rise, as a share of the top tier's open mouth (288 frame px) | | `layout` | `data-layout` | `auto` | `aside` or `list` to force one | | `align` | `data-align` | `true` | `false` keeps the panel at the top instead of level with the open tier | | `hash` | `data-hash` | `false` | `true` writes the chosen panel's id to the URL (`replaceState`) | Fewer than five panels: the tiers below the last tab stay closed under it (the demo's card has three). More than five are ignored: the box has five tiers. **Events** (bubbling, on the root): `jubako:change` `{index, id, tab, panel, by}`, `by` one of `tab`, `key`, `hand`, `api`. **API:** `const j = jubako(root)` → `j.select(i | id)`, `j.index`, `j.tabs`, `j.panels`, `j.hold(true|false)` and `j.advance(seconds)` (for stills), `j()` destroys (listeners, observers, the tablist it made; the page reads as it does without JS). Also on `root.jubako`. ## Theming `--paper --ink --ink-2 --ink-3 --rule --accent --serif --sans` as everywhere. Component custom properties: `--jb-box` (the box's width in the aside layout, default `clamp(280px, 31vw, 440px)`), `--jb-box-s` (in the list layout, `clamp(104px, 40%, 184px)`), `--jb-gutter` (room for the tabs beside the box, `13.5em`). The chosen tab's rule is `--accent`; the demo sets it to the red-brown of the box's own lacquered rims (#9a3b22). Japanese in a tab label uses `--jb-ja` (default Shippori Mincho, then Hiragino Mincho). ## In life, and here | In life | Here | |---|---| | A *jūbako* is a stack of square lacquered boxes, each fitting the one below, with a lid on top. At New Year *osechi* is packed into it a course to a tier, cooked beforehand so no fire is lit for the first three days, and stacked because good things should pile up: *ichi-no-jū* the celebratory small things, *ni-no-jū* the grilled, *san-no-jū* the simmered, then *yo-no-jū* (never *shi*, four, which also says death) the vinegared, and the fifth often left empty for the fortune still to come. | A stack of five tiers, one to a tab, the first tab the top tier: the demo's five tabs are those five tiers, the fifth "kept empty". Choosing a tab lifts every tier above it off, so the chosen tier's inside is open, as when you lift the upper tiers to reach the one you want. The lid (photographed in another campaign, against a different backdrop) is left off. | | The tiers sit flush, outer walls aligned, each fitting over the rim of the one below, so the seams read as fine dark lines in the decoration, with a glint of the lower tier's red rim. | Each tier is cut along its own bottom seam, found where two of the Met's photographs stop differing (residual 0.4 px), and runs to the box's two vanishing points. Stacked, each covers the inside of the one below, and the five photographs together match the first to 1.8 % mean difference. | | This box is black lacquer banded all round in stripes of gold and silver *hiramaki-e* (gold dust sprinkled into lacquer, low and flat), sheet lead, and *raden*, mother-of-pearl, with bands of scrolling arabesque between. The stripes run round the corners and across the seams, so the stack reads as one striped block. Its lid has Chinese figures in inlay. | The decoration is untouched: the Met's photographs at half their 4000 px scale, a registration resample (under a pixel for three tiers, 3 px and 18 px with a fraction of a degree for the last two) the only change. The stripes line up across every seam because every tier is the same lacquerer's band seen from the same camera. | | Inside, each tier is plain black lacquer with a red-brown rim, so food sits on black. | The insides you see open are the Met's: each tier's from the photograph in which it was on top. The undersides of lifted tiers never show (the camera looks down on them), so nothing has to be invented. | | The tiers are lifted straight up, by hand, and set down beside. A well-made tier fits so closely that the one below rises with it a moment before it lets go. | You can lift them by hand: hold a tier and draw it up, and everything above comes with it; let go and it settles open or back. The tier left behind rises a hair with the stack and drops back. The tiers hang rather than being set down beside, so the page doesn't reflow. The box's own photographed shadow stays on the floor under it; the lifted tiers cast none into the open tier, because no photograph shows that shadow and it would have to be drawn. | | Each course has its meanings: black beans for health, herring roe for children, prawns for a long life, lotus root for seeing ahead. Hiroshige's *Uozukushi* (Every Variety of Fish, 1830s) printed these same fish, with comic verses (*kyōka*) above them. | Each panel carries a real print of what its tier holds: Hiroshige's sea bream, spiny lobster, and black and red sea bream with bamboo shoots (the Met, CC0), and a surimono of a basket of lotus root (LACMA). The fifth tier's panel has none. | ## Files - `jubako.js` (about 450 lines), `jubako.css`: the component. No libraries. - `assets/tier-1.webp … tier-5.webp`, `assets/shadow.webp` (about 350 KB together), `assets/geometry.json`, `assets/credits.json`, `assets/PICK.md` (the hunt, the shortlist, which photograph covers which state, and why the gold-lined second box was left out). `assets/prints/` (the demo's four prints, about 700 KB, lazy-loaded). - `tools/cut.py`: register, matte, seams, export, from the Met originals. `tools/preview.py`: composite every state offline to check an export. ## Credits The box: *Food Box with Striped Decoration and Chinese Figures*, Japan, Edo period, 17th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2015.500.2.31a–f, Gift of Florence and Herbert Irving, 2015. Open Access, CC0. Photographs `L1996_47_86_O2_sf` … `O6_sf`. Prints: Utagawa Hiroshige, *Uozukushi*: "Medetai Fish and Sasaki Bamboo", "Ise-ebi and Shiba-ebi", "Kurodai and Kodai Fish with Bamboo Shoots and Berries" (The Met, DP123587, DP123581, DP123580; CC0). "Basket of Lotus Root and Single String Chin", surimono, Japan, 19th century (LACMA M.79.152.573, public domain). All via Wikimedia Commons. # jubako: the pick

Contact sheets (scratch, `tools/engine/jobs/`):
- `tabs-hunt/sheet-tiered-a.jpg`, `sheet-tiered-b.jpg`: every view of 27 Met tiered boxes, picnic sets, incense boxes,
  food boxes and stacked cases (188 tiles), found with the v1.1 search ("tiered food box", "tiered", "picnic set",
  "seal paste box", "nest of weights", "stacking", "compendium", "tiffin").
- `tabs-hunt/sheet-40343.jpg`: all twelve views of the box chosen.
- `tabs-hunt/sheet-jp-series.jpg`: the three other Met boxes photographed tier by tier (57965, 57966, 56528).
- `tabs-hunt/sheet-40258-444538.jpg`: the Ming mother-of-pearl tiered box (40258), the Mamluk brass box of Muhammad
  al-Hamawi (444538), a Chinese pewter tiered box (61280).
- `tabs-hunt/sheet-aic262426.jpg`: the Art Institute's Ming carved cinnabar four-tiered box (262426), six views.
- `tabs-commons/hunt/sheet.png`: Commons, 12 tiered boxes (Honolulu, British Museum, Okinawa, Yuan).
- `round9-lead-hunt/sheet-inro.jpg`: the lead's four inrō (58371, 58463, 58798, 58876).

`engine.py inspect --use hero` ran on all 26 originals fetched for the shortlist (`tabs-hunt/met/orig`). All pass: no
enlargement, full detail at 4000 px. One WARN (57966-4, near-perfect symmetry: a box seen square-on).

## The box: The Met 2015.500.2.31a–f, food box, Japan, 17th century

A tall square jūbako of five tiers in black lacquer, banded all round in stripes of gold and silver *hiramaki-e*, lead
and mother-of-pearl, with scrolling arabesque bands between; a lid (not used here) inlaid with Chinese figures. 27 cm
high. Gift of Florence and Herbert Irving, 2015. CC0.

**Why this one.** The Met photographed it in one campaign (`L1996_47_86_O*`, from its loan in 1996) **taken apart a
tier at a time from a fixed camera**: O2 the five tiers with the top one open, O3 with one tier lifted off, O4 with
two, O5 with three, O6 the bottom tier alone. That is exactly what a tab has to show: each state of the control is a
photograph. Difference images confirm the camera never moved: O3 and O4 register onto O2 within a pixel by
translation alone; O5 needs 3 px and 0.13 degrees, O6 18 px and 0.6 degrees (the bottom tier was nudged when the last
tier came off). After registration the bottom tier's band differs by 0.6 % (O3–O4) to 2 % (O6) of full scale, i.e. not
visibly at the half scale shipped.

Which photograph covers which state:

| part | photograph | what it shows that the others can't |
|---|---|---|
| tier 1 | O2 (all five) | tier 1's open inside, and its sides |
| tier 2 | O3 | tier 2's inside: in O2 it was under tier 1 |
| tier 3 | O4 | tier 3's inside |
| tier 4 | O5 | tier 4's inside |
| tier 5 | O6 | the bottom tier's inside, and the foot |
| shadow | O2 | the box's own shadow on the Met's backdrop |

Lifting tiers 1…k−1 off tier k shows nothing nobody photographed: tier k's inside is O(k+1)'s; the lifted tiers are seen
from above, so their undersides never show; and stacked, every tier covers the inside of the one below it exactly
(the stack composited from the five photographs matches O2 to 1.8 % mean absolute difference over the box, the
largest differences a pixel either side of the seams).

### Why not the others

| candidate | what it has | why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Met 40343, striped food box** | 5 tiers, photographed apart tier by tier, one camera | **picked** |
| Met 57965, incense box (jūkōgō), crest, pine, bamboo, plum | lid + 3 tiers, gold *nashiji* insides, apart tier by tier | 4 states only; the open views are cropped to different sizes (3238–3838 px wide), so each needs a scale fit as well. The runner-up, and a good second box (gold insides) |
| Met 57966, incense box, maple and raft | lid + 3 tiers apart, uncropped 4000 px, one camera | 4 states; small in frame (box ~1000 px wide) |
| Met 56528, jūbako with azaleas | 3 tiers + lid apart | 20th century; the open states vary in angle |
| Met 40258, Ming mother-of-pearl tiered box | four sides, top, an inside | no view apart: lifting a tier would show a rim nobody photographed |
| AIC 262426, Ming carved cinnabar four-tiered box | four sides straight on, top, superb | the same: never photographed apart |
| Met 61280/61281, Chinese tiered boxes | lid off beside | one state only |
| Met 444538, Mamluk brass box of Muhammad al-Hamawi | 10 views | not tiered (lidded) |
| Met 910102, three-tiered box in book form (1870s) | drawers out | drawers, 3 parts, Victorian |
| Met 57588 / 42624, sagejū picnic sets | every part laid out | parts laid flat on the table, not as a stack from one camera |
| Met inrō 58371, 58463, 58798, 58876 | sides, tops, cords | no tier ever photographed apart along its cords |
| Commons (Honolulu, BM, Okinawa, Yuan) | single gallery views | one state each |

**Japan, knowingly.** The brief asks for Japan only if nothing else is as good. Nothing else is: of 27 museum boxes and
12 Commons ones, only Japanese lacquer was photographed tier by tier, and this box best of all (five states, one
camera, 4000 px). Chinese tiered boxes (Ming cinnabar, Ming mother-of-pearl) are finer still as objects, but no
museum photographed them apart, and lifting a tier would need a rim drawn. The library has Japanese paper, prints
and katazome, but no lacquer (*maki-e*) and no stacked object.

## The cut (`tools/cut.py`)

1. **Register** O3–O6 onto O2 by the bottom tier's band (ECC; translation for O3–O4, affine for O5–O6).
2. **Matte** each state (BiRefNet via the asset engine, decontaminated edge).
3. **Seams.** On the left face, where O(n) and O(n+1) stop differing (taking a tier off changes everything above its
   bottom edge and nothing below): four lines with 0.4 px residual. The front edge read off the photograph at x = 1205
   (crop px; checked at the rim, every seam and the foot). The right face's difference is smeared by the lower tier's
   bright red rim, so each right seam runs from its corner to the right vanishing point, on the horizon the five left
   lines agree on (y = −2134) where the foot's right edge meets it. Checked: seam 1's slope from its own difference
   (−0.890) and from the vanishing point (−0.891) agree.
4. **Export** at half scale: each tier above its own bottom seam (1 px soft edge), the bottom tier whole, the
   shadow, `geometry.json`.

Not drawn, not stretched, not recoloured. The one resample is registration (sub-pixel to 0.6 degrees) and the halving.

## Round 9 rework (Connor: "could do with being more interesting")

**The prints in the panels.** The demo became a New Year osechi page, one tier per course, so each panel carries a
real print of what its tier holds. Hunted on Commons (`tools/engine/jobs/tabs-fish/hunt/sheet.png`, 19 candidates;
`tabs-veg/hunt/sheet.png`, 3), all `engine.py inspect` PASS:
- Hiroshige, *Uozukushi* (Every Variety of Fish), the Met's impressions (CC0): the sea bream with bamboo (*medetai*,
  the first tier), the spiny lobster and shrimp (prawns, the grilled tier), black and red sea bream with bamboo shoots
  (the simmered tier: *takenoko*). Chosen over his katsuo, aji and flatfish sheets because these are the fish (and the
  shoot) osechi actually holds.
- A 19th-century surimono of a basket of lotus root (LACMA M.79.152.573, public domain) for the vinegared tier
  (*su-renkon*). Hokusai/Hiroshige daikon and turnip sheets were looked for and not found in open collections.
- The fifth tier has no print: it is the tier kept empty.

**The second box, tried and set aside.** Met 57965, the 18th-century incense box (lid + 3 tiers, gold *nashiji* and a
bright gold-leaf bottom tier), photographed tier by tier: `tabs-hunt/sheet-57965-states.jpg`, scratch
`tools/engine/jobs/tabs-kogo/`. Its four states register by SIFT similarity (scale 1.005–1.013, rotation under 1
degree, 0.6 px residual on the bottom tier), but the bottom tier's band then differs by **4.4–6.9 %** between shots
(the striped box: 0.6–2 %) and the exposure moves by up to 8 % (the last shot is darker). Composited a tier from each
photograph, the seams would step in brightness; matching them would mean recolouring the photographs. Left out, on
the "untouched" rule. Diff maps: `tabs-kogo/diffs.jpg`.
